text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen nearly 9% over two weeks, with today's modest decline continuing a sharper drop that started around November 17th. The timing aligns with a major shift in refiner sentiment: on November 23rd, financial media explicitly reported that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating out of the sector after a long period of outsized gains. This shift appears to have outweighed any near-term support from geopolitical supply concerns (Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz) that would normally prop up oil prices and refinery margins.

The broader context is that refiners like this one have benefited enormously from wide profit margins over the past couple of years, but those conditions are normalizing. U.S. refineries are running at 95.7% capacity and storage levels are healthy across crude, gasoline, and diesel—there's no supply crisis pushing margins higher. Without the tailwind of exceptional profitability and amid a general cooling of energy enthusiasm (reflected in the climate summit headlines and shifting trader positioning), the stock is repricing downward even as geopolitical risks persist.
